--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/identity/authentication/concept-telephony-risk-based-captcha.md
@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
+---
+title: Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for telephony-based sign-in
+description: Learn about risk-based anti-bot verification before Microsoft Entra ID sends SMS messages or places voice calls for telephony-based sign-in.
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 10/14/2026
+ai-usage: ai-assisted
+# Customer intent: As an authentication administrator, I want to understand why users might see anti-bot verification before SMS or voice authentication and how to prepare my organization.
+---
+
+# Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for telephony-based sign-in
+
+Microsoft Entra ID uses safeguards to help reduce automated abuse of telephony-based sign-in. In some cases, users might be asked to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step, such as a CAPTCHA, before Microsoft sends an SMS message or places a voice call for sign-in. This safeguard helps protect against telephony fraud, such as International Revenue Share Fraud (IRSF).
+
+For more information about telephony fraud and how Microsoft helps limit the impact of fraudulent activity, see [Understanding telephony fraud risk](concept-mfa-telephony-fraud.md).
+
+## What anti-bot verification is
+
+The provider for this CAPTCHA experience is Arkose Labs. The challenge opens in a dialog during the authentication flow. The interaction helps confirm that the request is being made by a person before Microsoft sends an SMS message or places a voice call.
+
+The experience is risk-based and uses client behavior signals, so not every user or authentication attempt is affected. Microsoft doesn't publish the risk criteria or implementation details that determine when anti-bot verification is shown.
+
+## What users experience
+
+When anti-bot verification is required, the user must complete the verification step before Microsoft sends the SMS message or places the voice call. If the user can't complete the verification step, they should try again or use another available authentication method. If the CAPTCHA dialog doesn't load, your organization might need to allow the Arkose Labs domains. For more information, see [Network requirements](#network-requirements).
+
+Help desk teams should communicate that:
+
+- SMS and voice authentication aren't removed by this safeguard.
+- A user might need to complete an anti-bot verification step before receiving an SMS message or voice call.
+- If the verification step doesn't load, the issue might be related to network or firewall restrictions. For more information, see [Network requirements](#network-requirements).
+- Users should use another available non-telephony authentication method when possible. Non-telephony methods are more secure, aren't subject to this safeguard, and might provide a better user experience.
+
+## Network requirements
+
+Anti-bot verification can depend on resources that are loaded during the authentication flow. If an organization uses restrictive firewalls, proxies, or web filtering, users might be blocked from completing verification if the required endpoints aren't allowed.
+
+To allow the Arkose Labs verification challenge to load and complete during authentication, configure the firewall, proxy, or secure web gateway to permit outbound HTTPS traffic on TCP port 443 from users' devices to:
+
+- `*.arkoselabs.com`
+- `arkoselabs.com`
+
+Use your product's wildcard-domain or fully qualified domain name (FQDN) allowlist syntax so the rule covers all subdomains. Some products don't match the base domain with a wildcard entry, so add both domains.
+
+Also make sure that:
+
+- DNS filtering and web-content/category filtering policies don't block these domains, and that your allow rule takes priority over category-based blocks.
+- These domains are excluded from TLS/SSL inspection (HTTPS decryption), which can stop the challenge from loading or validating.
+
+## Prepare users and help desks
+
+To prepare for risk-based anti-bot verification:
+
+- Tell users that some SMS and voice authentication attempts might require anti-bot verification before Microsoft sends an SMS message or places a voice call.
+- Make sure help desk teams know that the verification step is expected when risk-based safeguards apply.
+- Review network requirements when the verification experience doesn't load.
+- Encourage users to register and use phishing-resistant authentication methods where possible, such as passkeys.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [SMS-based user sign-in for Microsoft Entra ID](howto-authentication-sms-signin.md)
+- [Voice call authentication method](concept-authentication-phone-options.md)
+- [Understanding telephony fraud risk for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication](concept-mfa-telephony-fraud.md)
+- [Troubleshoot MFA voice call and SMS problems](troubleshoot-voice-call-sms.md)
+- [Passkeys in Microsoft Entra ID](concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md)

newFiles.patch: diff --git a/docs/external-id/customers/how-to-invite-external-identity-provider-users-customers.md b/docs/external-id/customers/how-to-invite-external-identity-provider-users-customers.md new file mode 100644 index 00000000000..5f9b81058a0 --- /dev/null +++ b/docs/external-id/customers/how-to-invite-external-identity-provider-users-customers.md @@ -0,0 +1,133 @@ +--- +title: Route Invited Users to an External Identity Provider +description: Learn how to invite users to a Microsoft Entra external tenant and route them to a configured OpenID Connect, SAML/WS-Federation, or social identity provider. +author: nanguil +ms.author: nguilanians +ms.topic: how-to +ms.date: 10/12/2026 +ms.custom: it-pro, msecd-doc-authoring-1026 +ai-usage: ai-assisted + +#customer intent: As an IT admin or developer, I want to route invited users to a specific external identity provider so that they can access my application by using their existing credentials. +--- + +# Route invited users to an external identity provider + +[!INCLUDE [applies-to-external-only](../includes/applies-to-external-only.md)] + +You can invite consumers, business customers, and admins to a Microsoft Entra external tenant. By default, the [invitation redemption flow](../redemption-experience.md#invitation-redemption-flow) determines how an invited user authenticates. This article describes how to explicitly route an invited user to a configured external identity provider (IdP), such as a social provider, custom OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider, or Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML)/WS-Federation provider. + +Explicit identity provider routing is useful when: + +- Only invited users should be able to access your application (no self-service sign-up). +- Users must authenticate with a specific external identity provider. +- You want full control over the invitation experience and communication. + +Before you begin, ensure you have an external tenant, registered application, associated user flow, configured identity provider, and the provider's `domain_hint` value. + +## Prerequisites + +- A [Microsoft Entra External ID tenant](how-to-create-external-tenant-portal.md). +- A configured external identity provider: [Custom OIDC](how-to-custom-oidc-federation-customers.md), [Microsoft Entra ID](how-to-entra-id-federation-customers.md), [SAML/WS-Fed](../direct-federation.md), or a social provider ([Google](how-to-google-federation-customers.md), [Facebook](how-to-facebook-federation-customers.md), [Apple](how-to-apple-federation-customers.md)). +- A [registered application](/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app) in your external tenant. +- A [user flow](how-to-user-flow-sign-up-sign-in-customers.md) associated with your application. The user flow is required even if sign-up is disabled. You don't need to add the identity provider to the user flow when you route invited users by using `domain_hint`. +- The `domain_hint` value for the identity provider, as described in [Issuer acceleration](concept-authentication-methods-customers.md#issuer-acceleration). + +> [!IMPORTANT] +> The `domain_hint` parameter changes authentication routing during invitation redemption. It isn't required to invite a user, doesn't determine who is eligible for an invitation, and doesn't grant access to an application. When you use `domain_hint` to route a user from another Microsoft Entra tenant to custom OIDC federation, the sign-in doesn't use the native Microsoft Entra business-to-business (B2B) federation path or its home-tenant multifactor authentication (MFA) trust. + +## Disable self-service sign-up (optional) + +If you want only explicitly invited users to access your application, disable sign-up in your user flow. This prevents users who aren't invited from creating accounts through self-service registration. Your application still controls authorization for invited users. + +For detailed steps on finding your user flow ID and disabling sign-up, see [Disable sign-up in a user flow](how-to-disable-sign-up-user-flow.md). + +## Invite users + +You can invite users by using either the Microsoft Graph API or the admin center. Configure the invitation not to send the default email. Instead, send a custom email with an application link after you create the invitation (next step). + +Regardless of which option you use, when the invitation is created: + +- A user object is created in the external tenant with `externalUserState` set to `PendingAcceptance`. +- No identity provider is yet associated with the user object. + +> [!NOTE] +> Unlike self-service sign-up users, invited users aren't prompted for additional attributes during sign-in. Their user properties are based on the invitation and claims received from the external identity provider. + + + +### Option 1: Use the Microsoft Graph invitation API + +Create a user in the External ID tenant using the [Microsoft Graph Invitation API](/graph/api/invitation-post). + +```http +POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/invitations +Content-Type: application/json + +{ + "invitedUserEmailAddress": "user@contoso.com", + "inviteRedirectUrl": "https://your-app-url.com", + "sendInvitationMessage": false +} +``` + +### Option 2: Use the admin center + +You can also invite users through the Microsoft Entra admin center using the [Invite external user](~/fundamentals/how-to-create-delete-users.md#invite-an-external-user) option. To use this pattern, disable the default Microsoft invitation email and send your own custom invitation containing the `domain_hint` parameter as described in the next step. + +## Send a custom invitation email with the `domain_hint` parameter + +After creating the user, send your own email with a link to an application route that starts the External ID authorization request. Configure the application route to pass the `domain_hint` parameter in the authorization request so that External ID routes the user to the specified identity provider. + +The application route depends on your application. For example: + +```text +https:///?domain_hint= +``` + +Use the `domain_hint` value specified for your provider in [Issuer acceleration](concept-authentication-methods-customers.md#issuer-acceleration). For example, for custom OIDC, use the domain part of the issuer URI. For a Microsoft Entra ID tenant configured as a custom OIDC provider, use the tenant domain, such as `contoso.onmicrosoft.com`. + +Include this link in your custom invitation email. For example: + +> **Subject**: You're invited to access [Your Application Name] +> +> Hello, +> +> You've been invited to access [Your Application Name]. Select the following link to get started: +> +> [Accept invitation and sign in](https://your-app-url.com/signin?domain_hint=contoso.onmicrosoft.com) +> +> You'll be asked to sign in with your existing credentials. + +> [!NOTE] +> If you use the default Microsoft invitation email, the [invitation redemption flow](../redemption-experience.md#invitation-redemption-flow) determines how the user authenticates and might not route the user to your intended identity provider. + +## End-user experience + +After you complete the configuration and send the invitation, here's what the invited user experiences. + +### First sign-in (invitation redemption) + +1. The user receives your custom invitation email and selects the link that includes the `domain_hint` parameter. +1. The application starts the External ID authorization request with the `domain_hint` parameter, and the user is routed to the specified identity provider. +1. The user authenticates with their existing credentials at the identity provider. +1. The invitation is redeemed. In your external tenant, the user object is updated: + - A federated identity is added to the `identities` collection. + - The `externalUserState` changes to `Accepted`. + +> [!NOTE] +> The `domain_hint` parameter is only required during this initial invitation redemption step. + +### Subsequent sign-ins + +After the user completes invitation redemption: + +1. The user navigates to your application (no `domain_hint` parameter is needed). +1. The user enters their email address on the sign-in page. +1. The user is recognized as an existing user and is redirected to the identity provider used during invitation redemption. + +## Related content + +- [Create invitation (Microsoft Graph)](/graph/api/invitation-post) +- [Add and manage customer accounts](how-to-manage-customer-accounts.md) +- [Issuer acceleration](concept-authentication-methods-customers.md#issuer-acceleration)

diff --git a/docs/identity/devices/macos-platform-sso-architecture.md b/docs/identity/devices/macos-platform-sso-architecture.md
new file mode 100644
index 00000000000..effccb56e93
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/identity/devices/macos-platform-sso-architecture.md
@@ -0,0 +1,205 @@
+---
+title: "Architecture and authentication flow for macOS Platform SSO (Apple) with Microsoft Entra ID"
+description: "Understand how macOS Platform SSO registration, device keys, the Platform SSO PRT, app SSO, and Platform Credentials work with Microsoft Entra ID."
+ms.topic: concept-article
+ms.date: 10/14/2026
+---
+
+# Architecture and authentication flow for macOS Platform SSO (Apple) with Microsoft Entra ID
+
+macOS Platform Single Sign-on (PSSO) integrates a user's organizational identity with macOS. When PSSO is configured with Microsoft Entra ID, a managed Mac can establish a device-bound identity, register a local user, and provide single sign-on (SSO) to supported applications and websites.
+
+This article explains the architecture and authentication lifecycle behind that experience. It focuses on the responsibility boundaries between device management, macOS, the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in, Microsoft Entra ID, and applications.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> This article is a conceptual architecture overview. Exact behavior depends on the macOS version, the configured authentication method, the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in version, the mobile device management (MDM) configuration, and Microsoft Entra tenant policy.
+
+## Roles and responsibilities
+
+PSSO is an Apple platform capability implemented through an identity provider's SSO extension. It isn't a standalone Microsoft credential provider, and applications don't implement the device and user registration protocol themselves.
+
+With Microsoft Entra ID:
+
+- **The device management service** deploys the Extensible SSO policy and PSSO configuration.
+- **The Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in** registers the Mac and user with Microsoft Entra ID and supplies the identity-provider configuration required by macOS.
+- **macOS Platform SSO (Apple)** owns the operating-system experience. It invokes registration, protects platform credentials, coordinates authentication, and makes the resulting Platform SSO PRT available to the Microsoft SSO extension through Apple's supported framework.
+- **Microsoft Entra ID** registers the device and user credential, verifies the registered credential, validates the user and device proofs, and issues the Platform SSO Primary Refresh Token (PRT).
+- **Applications and browsers** request access to resources and receive only the tokens or sessions intended for them.
+
+[![Diagram that shows Platform SSO roles and responsibilities.](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-01-architecture.png)](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-01-architecture.png#lightbox)
+
+*Figure 1. Device management deploys PSSO, Microsoft registers the device and user, macOS orchestrates authentication, and applications benefit from SSO.*
+
+## Components
+
+| Component | Primary responsibility |
+| --- | --- |
+| Microsoft Intune or another supported MDM | Deploy the Extensible SSO configuration and select the PSSO authentication method |
+| Company Portal for macOS | Deliver the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in used for Microsoft Entra PSSO |
+| Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in | Perform Microsoft Entra device and user registration and provide identity-provider configuration to macOS |
+| macOS Platform SSO (Apple) | Coordinate registration and authentication, protect platform credentials, and integrate the organizational identity with macOS |
+| Microsoft Entra ID | Register the device and credential, verify the registered credential, validate the user and device proofs, and issue the Platform SSO PRT |
+| Secure Enclave | Protect device-bound keys and, with the UserSecureEnclaveKey method, the user-bound key |
+| Apps and browsers | Request resource tokens or web sessions backed by the Platform SSO foundation |
+
+## Policy deployment and device keys
+
+Before registration begins, the Mac receives an Extensible SSO configuration through MDM. The configuration identifies the SSO extension and contains the organization's PSSO settings, including the selected authentication method and registration behavior.
+
+When the device is MDM enrolled and the SSO extension policy with PSSO configuration is deployed, macOS generates two Secure Enclave-backed device keys:
+
+- **Device signing key:** Signs device-bound PSSO requests.
+- **Device encryption key:** Enables Microsoft Entra ID to protect responses so that only the registered Mac can recover them.
+
+This key-generation step occurs before Microsoft Entra device registration. Registration accesses the existing keys; it doesn't generate them as part of the service exchange. The private keys remain protected on the Mac and aren't exported to applications or Microsoft Entra ID.
+
+## Device registration
+
+Device registration establishes the Mac as a known Microsoft Entra device:
+
+1. macOS invokes the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in.
+2. macOS makes the previously generated device signing and encryption keys available through the PSSO framework.
+3. The extension creates device-registration proof and sends the required public-key material to Microsoft Entra ID.
+4. Microsoft Entra ID validates the request and creates or updates the device identity.
+5. Microsoft Entra ID returns a **registration certificate** associated with the device signing public key.
+6. The extension saves the registration certificate through the PSSO framework and completes registration.
+
+The registration certificate contains the device signing public key and binds it to the registered device identity. It isn't the private signing key and it isn't the user's authentication credential.
+
+## User registration
+
+User registration associates the local macOS user with a Microsoft Entra identity and provisions the authentication method selected by the administrator.
+
+The supported methods are:
+
+- Password
+- UserSecureEnclaveKey
+- Smart Card
+
+With the UserSecureEnclaveKey method, user registration also provisions a hardware-bound user key:
+
+1. The user completes Microsoft Entra authentication and any required multifactor authentication.
+2. macOS creates or accesses a user key protected by the Secure Enclave.
+3. The public key is registered with Microsoft Entra ID and associated with the user and device.
+4. The private key remains protected on the Mac.
+5. The extension completes the user's PSSO configuration.
+
+[![Diagram that shows the Platform SSO device and user registration sequence.](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-02-registration.png)](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-02-registration.png#lightbox)
+
+*Figure 2. Device registration establishes device trust; user registration associates a user and authentication method with the Mac.*
+
+## Identity-provider configuration
+
+After registration, the Microsoft extension supplies macOS with the configuration required to operate the Microsoft Entra authentication protocol. Conceptually, this configuration identifies:
+
+- The Microsoft Entra authority and endpoints.
+- The registered user.
+- The active authentication method.
+- The application, audience, and scopes used by the protocol.
+- The requirements for validating service responses.
+- The representation of method-specific authentication proof.
+
+macOS persists this information through Apple's PSSO framework. This arrangement allows macOS to coordinate login, unlock, account management, credential refresh, and System Settings experiences while Microsoft remains responsible for Microsoft Entra registration and service-specific validation.
+
+## Obtain the Platform SSO PRT
+
+The Microsoft Entra SSO credential used by PSSO is a hardware-bound PRT. The user proof differs by authentication method, but the high-level flow is shared:
+
+1. macOS determines that the Platform SSO PRT must be obtained or refreshed.
+2. macOS loads the identity-provider configuration saved during registration.
+3. macOS obtains anti-replay information from Microsoft Entra ID.
+4. macOS collects or invokes the configured user proof.
+5. macOS binds authentication to the registered device identity.
+6. Microsoft Entra ID verifies the registered credential and validates the user and device proofs.
+7. Microsoft Entra ID returns the Platform SSO PRT protected for the registered Mac.
+8. macOS decrypts, validates, and saves the Platform SSO PRT using operating-system protections.
+9. macOS makes the PRT available to the Microsoft SSO extension through Apple's PSSO framework.
+10. The extension uses the PRT to obtain app-specific tokens or complete supported web SSO.
+
+The user's password, private key used by UserSecureEnclaveKey, or smart-card private key isn't converted into a PRT. Those credentials prove the user's identity. Microsoft Entra ID issues the PRT after validating that proof and the registered device context.
+
+[![Diagram that shows how macOS obtains and protects the Platform SSO PRT.](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-03-authentication.png)](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-03-authentication.png#lightbox)
+
+*Figure 3. macOS sends the device-bound authentication request, protects the returned Platform SSO PRT, and shares it with the Microsoft SSO extension.*
+
+## Authentication methods
+
+The authentication method changes how the user proves identity. It doesn't change the broader device-registration and app-SSO architecture.
+
+### Password
+
+The Microsoft Entra password and local macOS password are synchronized according to PSSO policy. The authentication request remains bound to the registered Mac. This method reduces the number of passwords the user manages, but it isn't passwordless or phishing-resistant.
+
+### UserSecureEnclaveKey
+
+A hardware-bound user key is protected by the Secure Enclave. When fresh proof is required, macOS requests a signature from the private key and Microsoft Entra ID verifies it with the registered public key. The private key doesn't leave the Mac. The local account password remains a separate local credential.
+
+Microsoft recommends the UserSecureEnclaveKey auth method for most PSSO deployments.
+
+### SmartCard
+
+The user proves identity with a certificate and its associated private key. The user completes the required card and PIN interaction, and the smart card signs the authentication proof without exporting the private key. Microsoft Entra certificate-based authentication validates the certificate, signature, user mapping, registered device, and policy.
+
+[![Diagram that shows a comparison of Platform SSO authentication methods.](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-04-authentication-methods.png)](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-04-authentication-methods.png#lightbox)
+
+*Figure 4. Password, UserSecureEnclaveKey, and Smart Card are alternative methods for producing user authentication proof.*
+
+## Application and browser SSO
+
+Applications don't receive the user's private keys, registration certificate, or Platform SSO PRT.
+
+A supported app or browser starts a normal Microsoft Entra authentication operation. The Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in checks whether macOS has a compatible Platform SSO PRT. If one is available, the extension uses it to request an app-specific token or complete the supported web SSO flow.
+
+The resulting resource token remains scoped to the requesting client and resource. PSSO provides the reusable device and user authentication foundation; it doesn't give one application access to another application's tokens.
+
+[![Diagram that shows the Platform SSO application and browser sign-in sequence.](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-05-app-sso.png)](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-05-app-sso.png#lightbox)
+
+*Figure 5. The extension uses the Platform SSO PRT to complete SSO while each application receives only its own authorization.*
+
+## Platform Credentials and passkeys
+
+Platform Credential passkey authentication is an optional related capability. It isn't required to obtain or use the Platform SSO PRT.
+
+With supported Microsoft Entra scenarios, the Secure Enclave Platform Credential (Secure Enclave backed user key registered during PSSO with UserSecureEnclaveKey auth method) can answer a WebAuthn challenge:
+
+1. A browser or application receives a WebAuthn challenge from Microsoft Entra ID.
+2. macOS presents the eligible Platform Credential.
+3. The user completes verification, such as Touch ID when required.
+4. The Secure Enclave key signs the WebAuthn assertion.
+5. Microsoft Entra ID verifies the assertion using the registered public key.
+
+[![Diagram that shows Platform Credential passkey authentication.](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-06-passkey.png)](media/macos-platform-sso-architecture/platform-sso-public-06-passkey.png#lightbox)
+
+*Figure 6. A passkey operation uses the registered hardware-bound credential for WebAuthn without exporting its private key.*
+
+Routine PRT acquisition and passkey authentication can use the same registered hardware-backed identity, but they answer different protocol requests:
+
+- PSSO authentication obtains or refreshes the Platform SSO PRT.
+- Passkey authentication answers a WebAuthn challenge for a relying party.
+
+## Complete lifecycle
+
+The complete conceptual lifecycle is:
+
+1. MDM enrollment deploys the SSO extension policy and PSSO configuration.
+2. macOS generates the Secure Enclave-backed device signing and encryption keys.
+3. macOS invokes the extension for device registration.
+4. Microsoft Entra ID registers the device public keys and returns the device identity and registration certificate.
+5. macOS invokes user registration.
+6. The user registers the configured Password, UserSecureEnclaveKey, or Smart Card method.
+7. The extension saves the Microsoft Entra identity-provider configuration through Apple's PSSO framework.
+8. macOS obtains, validates, and protects the Platform SSO PRT.
+9. macOS shares the PRT with the Microsoft SSO extension through Apple's framework.
+10. Supported applications and browsers use the extension to obtain their own tokens or sessions.
+11. When policy requires new proof, macOS invokes the configured authentication method again.
+12. With UserSecureEnclaveKey, the Platform Credential can also answer supported WebAuthn passkey challenges.
+
+## Related content
+
+- [macOS Platform Single Sign-on (PSSO) overview](macos-psso.md)
+- [Configure Platform SSO for macOS devices in Microsoft Intune](/intune/device-configuration/settings-catalog/configure-platform-sso-macos)
+- [Configure Platform SSO during Automated Device Enrollment](/intune/device-configuration/settings-catalog/configure-platform-sso-during-enrollment)
+- [Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in for Apple devices](../../identity-platform/apple-sso-plugin.md)
+- [Apple Platform Single Sign-on deployment guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/deployment/platform-sso-for-mac-dep7bbb05313/web)
+- [Passkeys in Microsoft Entra ID](../authentication/concept-authentication-passkeys-fido2.md)
+- [Microsoft Entra certificate-based authentication on Apple devices](../authentication/concept-certificate-based-authentication-mobile-ios.md)

diff --git a/docs/identity/enterprise-apps/application-properties.md b/docs/identity/enterprise-apps/application-properties.md
index 17b4b944179..ad437659f94 100644
--- a/docs/identity/enterprise-apps/application-properties.md
+++ b/docs/identity/enterprise-apps/application-properties.md
@@ -3,7 +3,7 @@ title: 'Properties of an enterprise application'
 description: Learn about the properties of an enterprise application in Microsoft Entra ID.
 ms.topic: concept-article
 ai-usage: ai-assisted
-ms.date: 01/31/2025
+ms.date: 10/15/2026
 ms.reviewer: ergreenl
 ms.custom: enterprise-apps
 
@@ -14,12 +14,32 @@ ms.custom: enterprise-apps
 
 This article describes the properties that you can configure for an enterprise application in your Microsoft Entra tenant. To configure the properties, see [Configure enterprise application properties](add-application-portal-configure.md).
 
+## Activation status
+
+**Activation status** summarizes disablement conditions for the enterprise application. It shows **Deactivated** if any of the following conditions applies:
+
+- Sign-in is disabled for the service principal in your tenant (`accountEnabled=false`).
+- The app registration is deactivated (`isDisabled=true` on the app registration), which is reflected on the service principal.
+- Microsoft has disabled the application (`disabledByMicrosoftStatus=DisabledDueToViolationOfServicesAgreement`).
+
+The label alone doesn't identify which condition applies or prove that the app registration is deactivated. More than one condition can apply.
+
+| Condition | How to check | Guidance |
+|---|---|---|
+| Tenant-local sign-in disablement | Check **Enabled for users to sign-in?** on the enterprise application's **Properties** page, or read the service principal's `accountEnabled` property in Microsoft Graph. | Review why sign-in was disabled before restoring it. To restore tenant-local sign-in, set **Enabled for users to sign-in?** to **Yes** and save, or set `accountEnabled=true`. See [Disable user sign-in](disable-user-sign-in-portal.md). |
+| App registration deactivation | Check the app registration's **State** in its home tenant, or read the application object's `isDisabled` property in Microsoft Graph. | An authorized administrator in the application's home tenant can [reactivate the app registration](deactivate-app-registration.md#reactivate-an-application). |
+| Microsoft disablement | Read the service principal's `disabledByMicrosoftStatus` property in Microsoft Graph. | See [Protect against consent phishing](protect-against-consent-phishing.md#recommended-response-and-remediation) for investigation and remediation guidance. |
+
+You need appropriate permissions in the tenant where you make a change. Enabling tenant-local sign-in doesn't override app registration deactivation or Microsoft disablement. Reactivating the app registration doesn't enable a service principal whose `accountEnabled` remains `false`.
+
 ## Enabled for users to sign in?
 
 If this option is set to **Yes**, then assigned users are able to sign in to the application from the My Apps portal, the User access URL, or by navigating to the application URL directly. If assignment is required, then only users who are assigned to the application are able to sign-in. If assignment is required, applications must be assigned to get a token.
 
 If this option is set to **No**, then no users are able to sign in to the application, even if they're assigned to it. Tokens aren't issued for the application. This setting not only prevents users from signing in but also restricts service principals from accessing the application using application permissions.
 
+This setting maps to the service principal's `accountEnabled` property in your tenant. Setting it to **No** (`accountEnabled=false`) also makes **Activation status** show **Deactivated**, even if the app registration isn't deactivated. For instructions, see [Disable user sign-in for an application](disable-user-sign-in-portal.md).
+
 ## Name
 
 This property is the name of the application that users see on the My Apps portal. Administrators see the name when they manage access to the application. Other tenants see the name when integrating the application into their directory.

@@ -120,9 +120,9 @@ This risk detection type indicates sign-ins from an anonymous IP address (for ex
 
 This risk detection type identifies two sign-ins originating from geographically distant locations, where at least one of the locations might also be atypical for the user, given past behavior. The algorithm takes into account multiple factors including the time between the two sign-ins and the time it would take for the user to travel from the first location to the second. This risk might indicate that a different user is using the same credentials. 
 
-The algorithm ignores obvious "false positives" contributing to the impossible travel conditions, such as VPNs and locations regularly used by other users in the organization. The system has an initial learning period of the earliest of 14 days or 10 logins, during which it learns a new user's sign-in behavior. 
+The system uses adaptive learning to learn a new user's sign-in behavior.
 
-- Calculated offline
+- Calculated in real-time
 - License requirement: Microsoft Entra ID P2

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Purview | Information Protection: Sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra security groups
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Purview will enable sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups starting mid-November 2026, allowing administrators to apply and enforce governance policies on these groups. Labels can be assigned via multiple platforms, cannot yet be changed once applied, and require separate tenant configuration from Microsoft 365 groups.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

Microsoft Purview is introducing sensitivity labels for Microsoft Entra cloud security groups. This capability extends label-based protection currently available for Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites to cloud security groups.

With this change, organizations can apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels directly to security groups and automatically enforce membership and guest access policies when groups are created or labeled. This helps administrators apply governance policies consistently across group types, reduce the risk of oversharing, and support controlled self-service group creation.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 568217.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 and expected to complete in late November 2026

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Entra administrators
  • Microsoft Purview administrators
  • Organizations that use or plan to use sensitivity labels to govern access to Microsoft Entra security groups

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview
  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Microsoft Entra admin center
  • Azure portal
  • Microsoft Graph
  • PowerShell

What will happen

  • Administrators will be able to apply published Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to cloud security groups during group creation or after a group has been created.
  • Labels can be assigned through the Microsoft Entra admin center, Azure portal, PowerShell, or Microsoft Graph.
  • Existing sensitivity label functionality for Microsoft 365 groups will remain unchanged.
  • Once a sensitivity label is applied to a security group, the label cannot currently be changed or removed. Support for changing assigned labels will be introduced in a future update.
  • Sensitivity labels can be used to enforce organizational membership and guest access policies for security groups.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required to receive this change.

  • To use sensitivity labels with Microsoft Entra security groups after rollout:
  • Confirm that your organization has eligible licensing, such as Microsoft 365 E3 or Microsoft 365 E5, which includes Microsoft Entra ID P1.
  • In the Microsoft Purview portal, publish the sensitivity labels you want to use with the Groups & Sites scope enabled.
  • Allow up to 24 hours for labels to synchronize and become available in Microsoft Entra ID.
  • Enable sensitivity label support for cloud security groups in your tenant settings.
  • If sensitivity labels are already enabled for Microsoft 365 groups, note that cloud security groups require a separate configuration setting and must be enabled independently.

Consider reviewing your existing sensitivity label policies and governance processes before enabling this feature, particularly because assigned labels cannot currently be changed or removed from security groups.

Learn more

  • Assign sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra security groups | Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Learn about sensitivity labels | Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn
  • Use sensitivity labels to protect collaborative workspaces (groups and sites) | Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

QuestionAnswer
Does the change modify or add to Purview-related capabilities?Yes. This update extends Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels to Microsoft Entra security groups, adding a new governance and protection capability for this group type.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators must enable sensitivity label support for cloud security groups and manage label publication and assignment through Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Entra administrative controls.
Does the change alter how admins manage or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Administrators can use sensitivity labels on cloud security groups to apply and enforce access governance policies, expanding the scope of compliance controls available within Microsoft Purview.
